title: Outposts and open files
intro: Where do your pieces belong after the opening? Knights on outposts, rooks on open files and the 7th rank.

lessons.title: Outposts for knights
lessons.summary: A square no enemy pawn can ever attack.

steps.text: An outpost is a square in your opponent's half that their pawns can never attack. A knight there cannot be chased away.
Black's pawns on d6 and e5 can only move forward, and there is no black pawn left on the c- or e-file behind them. So nothing can ever push your knight off d5.
From d5 the knight eyes c7, e7, f6 and b6, deep in Black's camp.
Black has no f-pawn, and the d-pawn has passed e5. Put your knight on its outpost.
steps.hint: Which square in Black's half can no black pawn attack? Your d4 pawn supports it.
steps.ifWrong: Find a square in Black's half that your d4 pawn protects and no black pawn can attack.
steps.ifRight: A knight on e5, supported by d4, attacking d7 and more.

lessons.title: Open files and the 7th rank
lessons.summary: Rooks want open lines, and the 7th row is their favourite target.

steps.text: An open file has no pawns on it. A rook on an open file can travel all the way to the 7th rank, where the enemy pawns stand.
Before your rook leaves, check your own back row. Your pawn on h3 gives the king an escape square (called luft), so a rook check on your first row is not mate.
Take the open file to the 7th rank.
steps.hint: The e-file is open all the way.
steps.ifWrong: Use the open e-file to reach the 7th rank.
steps.ifRight: The rook attacks b7 and f7 at once.
